## History
[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=House_of_Nicolas_Flamel&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]
[Nicolas Flamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicolas_Flamel "Nicolas Flamel"), a wealthy member of the Parisian [bourgeoisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bourgeoisie "Bourgeoisie"), commissioned the house after the death of his wife Pernelle in 1397, to accommodate the homeless.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-Mignot-2) It was completed in 1407, as is inscribed on a [frieze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frieze "Frieze") above the ground floor, and it is the best known and sole surviving of Flamel's houses, yet he actually never lived there. The house is probably the oldest in Paris.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-M%C3%A9rim%C3%A9e-1)
The house's [facade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facade "Facade") became a _[monument historique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_historique "Monument historique")_[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-M%C3%A9rim%C3%A9e-1)
The building is currently[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] used as a private home and a restaurant, the _Auberge Nicolas Flamel_[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Nicolas_Flamel#cite_note-Lib%C3%A9-3)
